edges.description: The lengthened polyalanine tract renders PABPN1 aggregation-prone, so the expanded protein misfolds and accumulates as insoluble oligomers rather than remaining dispersed in the nucleoplasm.
The insoluble inclusions act as a sink, trapping poly(A) RNA together with ubiquitin, proteasome subunits and chaperones.
edges.target: Sequestration of Poly(A) RNA and Proteostasis Machinery

edges.description: Accumulating intranuclear aggregate burden in eyelid, pharyngeal and limb girdle muscle fibres accompanies the myopathic, rimmed-vacuolar changes of OPMD. Inclusion frequency correlates with the number of abnormal alleles.
The aggregates formed at this node are what a muscle biopsy shows as intranuclear inclusions.
Loss of normal nuclear poly(A) RNA handling and of proteostasis capacity in affected myonuclei accompanies the progressive myopathy.
edges.source: Sequestration of Poly(A) RNA and Proteostasis Machinery

edges.description: Degeneration of the levator palpebrae superioris produces the progressive bilateral eyelid droop that is usually the presenting sign.
Degeneration of the pharyngeal musculature, with failure of cricopharyngeal relaxation, produces progressive oropharyngeal dysphagia.
Later involvement of limb girdle musculature, predominantly proximal and lower limb, follows the oculopharyngeal onset.
Degeneration of trunk and neck musculature produces axial weakness as the disease progresses.
Involvement of facial muscles extends the cranial muscle weakness beyond the eyelids.
Involvement of the pharyngeal and laryngeal musculature produces the characteristic wet voice.
Respiratory muscle involvement puts patients at risk of hypoventilation during sleep; the mediating muscles are not specified by the source.
Impaired pharyngeal clearance allows food and secretions into the airway.

nodes.description: Pneumonia following aspiration of food or secretions past an incompetent pharynx. It is the principal life-threatening complication of OPMD.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Swallowing difficulties, which determine prognosis, increase the risk for potentially life-threatening aspiration pneumonia and poor nutrition.

nodes.description: Weakness of neck and trunk muscles, a later manifestation reported alongside limb girdle weakness in OPMD cohorts.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Other manifestations as the disease progresses can include limitation of upward gaze, tongue atrophy and weakness, chewing difficulties, wet voice, facial muscle weakness, axial muscle weakness, and proximal limb girdle weakness predominantly in lower limbs.

evidence.reference_title: Intranuclear Aggregates Precede Clinical Onset in Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: In addition to the characteristic OPMD symptoms including ptosis and dysphagia, other symptoms such as limb girdle and axial weakness, and external ophthalmoplegia were frequently observed.

nodes.description: Division of the cricopharyngeus to relieve oropharyngeal dysphagia. In a retrospective series of 39 patients, extramucosal myotomy achieved complete remission or marked improvement in 35, but about one third of those improved later relapsed, and revision by transmucosal endoscopic myotomy is an option.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term results of cricopharyngeal myotomy in oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: In the short term, 25 patients showed a complete remission of symptoms, 10 showed a marked improvement, and 4 exhibited no improvement at all (success rate of 90%).

nodes.description: Texture and consistency modification of the diet is the first-line management of OPMD dysphagia, with surgery reserved for symptomatic dysphagia that materially affects quality of life.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: The initial treatment for dysphagia is dietary modification; surgical intervention for dysphagia should be considered when symptomatic dysphagia has a significant impact on quality of life.

nodes.description: Progressive oropharyngeal swallowing difficulty with a mean onset around age 50. Dysphagia determines prognosis in OPMD because it drives aspiration pneumonia and malnutrition.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Swallowing difficulties, which determine prognosis, increase the risk for potentially life-threatening aspiration pneumonia and poor nutrition.

nodes.description: A wet voice from pharyngeal and laryngeal involvement, one of the later bulbar features alongside tongue atrophy and chewing difficulty.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Other manifestations as the disease progresses can include limitation of upward gaze, tongue atrophy and weakness, chewing difficulties, wet voice, facial muscle weakness, axial muscle weakness, and proximal limb girdle weakness predominantly in lower limbs.

nodes.description: Tubulofilamentous intranuclear inclusions about 8.5 nm in outer diameter within myonuclei, containing PABPN1 and p62. They are present in every OPMD muscle biopsy and are regarded as pathognomonic.

evidence.reference_title: Intranuclear inclusions in oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy among Bukhara Jews.
evidence.snippet: Typical tubulofilamentous intranuclear inclusions (INI) of 8.5 nm outer diameter were present in all cases.

evidence.reference_title: Intranuclear inclusions in muscle biopsy can differentiate oculopharyngodistal myopathy and oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: the myo-INIs were found in all of the patients (100%, 15/15)

nodes.description: Hypoventilation during sleep. GeneReviews names it as a risk warranting routine respiratory surveillance; it does not give a frequency.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: respiratory function given the increased risk for both aspiration and nocturnal hypoventilation

evidence.reference_title: Short GCG expansions in the PABP2 gene cause oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: A (GCG)6 repeat encoding a polyalanine tract located at the N terminus of the protein was expanded to (GCG)8-13 in the 144 OPMD families screened.

evidence.snippet: Both forms are caused by short (GCG)8-13 expansions in the polyadenylate-binding protein nuclear 1 gene (PABPN1) located on chromosome 14q11.1.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy: phenotypic and genotypic studies in a UK population.
evidence.snippet: Patients with longer repeat lengths, such as (GCG)(13), developed severe limb weakness early in the disease.

nodes.description: Expanded PABPN1 misfolds and self-associates into insoluble, tubulofilamentous intranuclear inclusions roughly 8.5 nm in outer diameter within skeletal muscle fibre nuclei. These inclusions are the pathological hallmark of OPMD, are decorated by anti-PABPN1 antibodies, and contain a salt-extraction-resistant form of the protein. They appear in muscle biopsies of presymptomatic Ala-expanded PABPN1 carriers, placing aggregation upstream of clinical weakness.

evidence.reference_title: Nuclear inclusions in oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy consist of poly(A) binding protein 2 aggregates which sequester poly(A) RNA.
evidence.snippet: This suggests that the polyalanine expansions in PABP2 induce a misfolding and aggregation of the protein into insoluble inclusions, similarly to events in neurodegenerative diseases caused by CAG/polyglutamine expansions.

evidence.reference_title: Nuclear inclusions in oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy consist of poly(A) binding protein 2 aggregates which sequester poly(A) RNA.
evidence.snippet: In this work we report that PABP2 is detected in filamentous nuclear inclusions, which are the pathological hallmark of OPMD.

evidence.snippet: Typical tubulofilamentous intranuclear inclusions (INI) of 8.5 nm outer diameter were present in all cases.

evidence.reference_title: Intranuclear Aggregates Precede Clinical Onset in Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: This indicates that the expression of Ala-expanded-PABPN1 causes the formation of nuclear aggregates before the onset of muscle weakness.

nodes.description: A short GCN (GCG) trinucleotide repeat in the first exon of PABPN1 expands from the normal (GCG)6 to (GCG)8-13, lengthening the N-terminal polyalanine tract of the nuclear poly(A)-binding protein. PABPN1 normally binds nascent poly(A) tails with high affinity and controls their extension and length, so the lesion falls on a protein with a defined nuclear RNA-processing role.

evidence.reference_title: Short GCG expansions in the PABP2 gene cause oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: A (GCG)6 repeat encoding a polyalanine tract located at the N terminus of the protein was expanded to (GCG)8-13 in the 144 OPMD families screened.

evidence.snippet: The mutations cause the lengthening of an N-terminal polyalanine domain.

evidence.reference_title: Nuclear inclusions in oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy consist of poly(A) binding protein 2 aggregates which sequester poly(A) RNA.
evidence.snippet: This gene encodes the poly(A) binding protein 2 (PABP2), an abundant nuclear protein that binds with high affinity to nascent poly(A) tails, stimulating their extension and controlling their length.

nodes.description: Physiotherapy, occupational therapy and assistive devices for falls prevention and mobility as limb girdle weakness progresses.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Physical and occupational therapy are encouraged; assistive devices may be necessary to prevent falls and assist with walking and mobility.

nodes.description: Limb girdle weakness, predominantly proximal and affecting the lower limbs more than the upper, developing after the oculopharyngeal features. Some severely affected individuals eventually require a wheelchair. This proximal predominance is the clinical feature that most usefully separates OPMD from oculopharyngodistal myopathy.

evidence.snippet: It is also clinically characterized by oculopharyngeal muscle involvement and rimmed vacuolar pathology, but the associated limb muscle weakness is typically proximal, rather than distal

nodes.description: Progressive, usually bilateral drooping of the eyelids from levator palpebrae involvement. It is the first reported symptom in about two-thirds of patients and has a mean age of onset around 48 years.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy: phenotypic and genotypic studies in a UK population.
evidence.snippet: Ptosis was the first reported symptom in two-thirds of the patients, and half of the subjects studied had evidence of ophthalmoplegia.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: the mean age of onset of ptosis is usually 48 years and of dysphagia 50 years

nodes.description: Blepharoplasty by levator aponeurosis resection, or frontalis suspension of the eyelids when levator function is poor. In a series of 92 OPMD patients, two polypropylene frontalis suspension techniques produced an equivalent gain in margin reflex distance.

evidence.reference_title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Treatment for ptosis may include blepharoplasty by either resection of the levator palpebrea aponeurosis or frontal suspension of the eyelids.

nodes.description: The intranuclear inclusions trap poly(A) mRNA together with ubiquitin, proteasome subunits and the chaperones HSP40 and HSP70. Sequestering both the RNA cargo of PABPN1 and the machinery that would normally clear misfolded protein is the proposed route by which aggregation becomes toxic, potentially interfering with nuclear export of poly(A) RNA.

nodes.description: Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle fibres with rimmed vacuoles and myopathic change, selectively and earliest affecting the levator palpebrae and pharyngeal musculature and later the limb girdles, predominantly proximally and in the lower limbs. In OPMD roughly one in eight myonuclei carries a p62-positive intranuclear inclusion, a far higher burden than in other rimmed-vacuolar myopathies.
